cocktails.name: Port Au Prince
cocktails.description: A vibrant Haitian-inspired rum punch bursting with pineapple and spice.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice. Garnish with a pineapple spear and mint sprig.
cocktails.story: Martin Cate's take on this classic draws from mid-century tiki traditions, evoking the exotic ports of Haiti where rum flowed freely. Created as a nod to the island's vibrant culture, the name references Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital. Bartenders love telling guests it's a 'sailor's delight'—strong enough to weather any storm but bright enough to make you forget the waves. A perfect introduction to allspice dram's warm complexity.

cocktails.name: Halekulani Cocktail
cocktails.description: A refined 1930s Waikiki classic blending bourbon with tropical brightness.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and double-strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with an edible orchid.
cocktails.story: Originating from the House Without a Key lounge at the Halekulani Hotel in Waikiki during the 1930s, this elegant sipper was adapted by Martin Cate from Beachbum Berry's research. It captures the golden era of Hawaiian tourism when Hollywood stars escaped to paradise. The name means 'House of Heaven'—a fitting tribute. Guests always smile when you mention it was a favorite of those seeking sophistication amid the tiki boom.

cocktails.name: Sidewinder's Fang
cocktails.description: A potent, snake-bite sharp blend of rums and citrus with a venomous kick.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained into a tiki mug. Garnish with mint and a lime wheel.
cocktails.story: This Don the Beachcomber classic gets its fierce name from the 'sidewinder'—a deadly desert rattlesnake—symbolizing its sneaky potency. Revived and refined at Smuggler's Cove, it's a golden-era powerhouse. Legend has it Donn Beach created many such 'fangs' to keep Hollywood's elite entertained (and slightly off-balance). Tell guests it's 'one bite and you're hooked'—they'll order another round instantly.

cocktails.name: Formidable Dragon
cocktails.description: A formidable beast of molasses, honey, and powerful rums.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice, strain into a glass over crushed ice, Top with soda water. Garnish with mint and lemon wheel. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: Crafted for a 2015 tiki event, this Smuggler's Cove original honors British Admiral Edward Vernon (Old Grog) and naval rum traditions. The 'dragon' refers to its fiery strength and mythical allure. Martin Cate uses it to illustrate tiki's blend of history and theater. Guests love the tale of how it 'breathes fire'—a nod to the potent rum blend that sneaks up like a dragon at sea.

cocktails.name: Hana Reviver
cocktails.description: A revitalizing floral and herbal tiki reviver from paradise.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a chilled coupe or tiki glass. Garnish with edible flowers and mint.
cocktails.story: This Smuggler's Cove creation captures the spirit of Hana, Maui—a hidden paradise. It revives the drinker with bright, restorative notes inspired by Hawaiian botanicals and tiki revival ingenuity. Martin Cate uses it to showcase how modern tiki honors place and history. Tell guests it's 'the cure for whatever ails you after a long sail.'

cocktails.name: Aku Aku
cocktails.description: A mysterious, creamy almond-coconut tiki classic with deep rum character.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained into a tiki mug. Garnish with mint and pineapple.
cocktails.story: Named after the famous 1930s film and book that popularized Polynesian mystique, this Don the Beachcomber creation was revived by Martin Cate. It captures the escapist fantasy of early tiki—guests feel transported to a hidden South Seas lagoon. The name 'Aku Aku' refers to guardian spirits; bartenders love whispering that one sip summons good fortune (and maybe a second round).

cocktails.name: Hawaiian Sunset
cocktails.description: A glowing sunset of pineapple, grenadine, and smooth rums.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a tall glass with crushed ice, layering grenadine at bottom. Garnish with pineapple and cherry.
cocktails.story: Evoking those magical Hawaiian evenings, this golden-era beauty layers colors like the sky over Waikiki. Adapted at Smuggler's Cove, it's a visual and flavorful stunner. The story always delights guests: 'Watch it change hues just like the islands at dusk.'

cocktails.name: Lei Lani Volcano
cocktails.description: A floral eruption of passion fruit, rum, and volcanic spice.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tiki glass over crushed ice. Garnish with orchid and mint.
cocktails.story: Modern Smuggler's Cove creation inspired by Hawaiian leis and explosive tiki theatrics. The 'volcano' refers to its layered intensity. Martin Cate uses it to showcase how tiki evolves—beautiful, fragrant, and memorably potent. Guests love the story of it 'erupting' with flavor.

cocktails.name: Tradewinds
cocktails.description: Smooth coconut and apricot winds carrying rich Jamaican rums.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and a paper umbrella.
cocktails.story: A 1970s Jamaican-inspired drink revived by Beachbum Berry and polished at Smuggler's Cove. It evokes the steady trade winds that powered sailing ships across the Caribbean. The creamy apricot note makes it a charter favorite—'smooth sailing in a glass.'

cocktails.name: Swizzle Français
cocktails.description: A French-Caribbean swizzle with agricole rum and Chartreuse elegance.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a Collins glass with crushed ice. Swizzle vigorously. Garnish with mint and nutmeg.
cocktails.story: Martin Cate's modern tribute blending Martinique rhum agricole with herbal French liqueurs. It bridges tiki and classic cocktail worlds. The swizzle technique is pure theater—guests are mesmerized as you spin the drink into a frosty masterpiece.

cocktails.name: The Undead Gentleman
cocktails.description: A sophisticated Zombie cousin with absinthe elegance.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour into a tiki mug. Float absinthe. Garnish with mint.
cocktails.story: Smuggler's Cove's refined take on the undead tiki legend. It's 'gentlemanly' in balance but still dangerously potent. The story ties back to Donn Beach's wild originals—perfect for telling tales of tiki's rebellious past while serving something polished.

cocktails.name: Don's Own Grog
cocktails.description: Don the Beachcomber's personal grog — bold, honeyed, and refreshingly potent.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice. Garnish with lime wheel and mint.
cocktails.story: This was Donn Beach's own go-to variation of the classic Navy Grog. Martin Cate revived it as a tribute to the father of tiki. The name honors the man who started it all in the 1930s. Bartenders tell guests it's the drink that kept Donn creative through long Hollywood nights — strong enough to fuel genius, balanced enough to enjoy.

cocktails.name: Mundo Perdido
cocktails.description: Jeff Berry's lost-world creation of apple brandy and dark rum.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a coupe or rocks glass. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created exclusively for Smuggler's Cove by Jeff “Beachbum” Berry in 2009. “Mundo Perdido” (Lost World) evokes forgotten tropical paradises. It's a modern classic that bridges old and new tiki. Guests enjoy hearing how it was designed as a lighter, more approachable tiki drink.

cocktails.name: Twenty Seventy Swizzle
cocktails.description: A high-octane swizzle named for its potent 127-proof rum.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a Collins glass with crushed ice and swizzle vigorously. Garnish with mint, nutmeg, and swizzle stick.
cocktails.story: A modern Smuggler's Cove powerhouse that nods to overproof rum's strength. The name references the 127 proof of the black rum used. It's become legendary for its balance and the theatrical swizzle ritual. Perfect for telling guests it's “strong enough to launch you into the stars.”

cocktails.name: The Dead Reckoning
cocktails.description: A complex navigation of rums, amaro, and citrus precision.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained into a tiki mug. Garnish with mint.
cocktails.story: Smuggler's Cove's modern classic named after the nautical art of dead reckoning. It rewards careful balancing of strong ingredients — much like plotting a course. Martin Cate uses it to illustrate tiki's precision beneath the fun. Tell guests it's the drink that always finds its way home.

cocktails.name: Kaiteur Swizzle
cocktails.description: A Guyanese-inspired powerhouse swizzle honoring mighty falls.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a tall glass with crushed ice and swizzle well. Garnish with lime and nutmeg.
cocktails.story: Inspired by Guyana's spectacular Kaiteur Falls, this bold Demerara swizzle celebrates the power of premium rum. Smuggler's Cove version highlights heritage while delivering refreshing drinkability. The swizzle action mimics cascading water — pure tiki theater.

cocktails.name: Chartreuse Swizzle
cocktails.description: A vibrant green swizzle marrying Chartreuse and island spices.
cocktails.instructions: Build in Collins glass with crushed ice. Swizzle thoroughly. Garnish with mint and lime.
cocktails.story: Smuggler's Cove's elegant fusion of French herbal tradition with Caribbean swizzle technique. It showcases tiki's willingness to embrace the world's best ingredients. The brilliant color always sparks conversation — 'the jungle comes alive in your glass.'

cocktails.name: Port Light
cocktails.description: Trader Vic's bourbon beauty with passion fruit and honey brightness.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a rocks glass over crushed ice. Garnish with a cherry and orange wheel.
cocktails.story: A Trader Vic classic from the golden era, the Port Light showcases bourbon's place in tiki alongside rum. Martin Cate's adaptation highlights its elegant balance. The name evokes a welcoming harbor light — perfect for guiding guests into tiki paradise. It's a favorite for showing that tiki isn't just rum.

cocktails.name: Demerara Dry Float
cocktails.description: Don the Beachcomber's dry, potent Demerara rum float.
cocktails.instructions: Shake base ingredients with ice and strain into a glass with crushed ice. Float Demerara rum on top. Garnish with lime.
cocktails.story: A Don the Beachcomber original emphasizing the rich, earthy character of Demerara rums. Revived at Smuggler's Cove, it showcases early tiki's love of bold, unadorned rum. The 'dry float' refers to the technique of floating heavier rum on top. Bartenders call it a 'sailor's handshake' — straightforward and strong.

cocktails.name: Mexican El Diablo
cocktails.description: Trader Vic's fiery tequila-ginger devil with lime and cassis.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a tall glass with ice. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: A Trader Vic creation that cleverly brings tequila into the tiki fold. The name 'El Diablo' (The Devil) warns of its sneaky heat from ginger beer. Martin Cate includes it as an example of tiki's global influences. Guests always grin when you say it's 'the devil you want to dance with.'

cocktails.name: Singapore Sling (Trader Vic)
cocktails.description: Trader Vic's tiki-fied version of the classic Singapore Sling.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over ice. Garnish with cherry and orange.
cocktails.story: Trader Vic adapted this famous Raffles Hotel drink for the American tiki scene. Martin Cate presents it as a bridge between classic cocktails and exotic tiki. The vibrant pink color and layered flavors made it a Hollywood favorite. Tell guests it's the sling that launched a thousand toasts.

cocktails.name: Tiki Bowl
cocktails.description: Don the Beachcomber's legendary communal sharing bowl.
cocktails.instructions: Blend ingredients with ice and pour into a tall glass. Garnish lavishly with fruit and flowers. Serve with long straws. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: One of Don the Beachcomber's iconic large-format drinks designed for groups. It embodies tiki's communal spirit. Smuggler's Cove version keeps the fun and theater alive. The story of friends passing the bowl around a table is pure tiki magic — ideal for your charter crew or guests.

cocktails.name: Hurricane
cocktails.description: Trader Vic's powerful passion fruit rum hurricane.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over crushed ice. Garnish with orange and cherry.
cocktails.story: Trader Vic's take on the New Orleans classic, adapted for tiki with extra rum power. It captures the wild energy of a tropical storm. Martin Cate includes it as a fun, shareable crowd-pleaser. The name guarantees smiles — 'it hits like a hurricane but tastes like paradise.'

cocktails.name: Scorpion
cocktails.description: Don the Beachcomber's famous communal Scorpion Bowl.
cocktails.instructions: Blend with ice and serve in a tall glass. Garnish with flowers and fruit. Share with straws. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: A legendary large-format drink from Don the Beachcomber, meant for sharing among friends. The 'scorpion' sting comes from its deceptive strength. Smuggler's Cove keeps the tradition alive for groups. It's the ultimate icebreaker — one bowl, many stories.

cocktails.name: Pupule
cocktails.description: Don the Beachcomber's wild 'crazy' multi-rum passion fruit punch.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over crushed ice. Garnish with pineapple spear and cherry.
cocktails.story: A Don the Beachcomber original whose name means 'crazy' in Hawaiian. It perfectly captures the wild, uninhibited spirit of early tiki. Smugglers Cove's version keeps the potent multi-rum profile while ensuring balance. Bartenders love telling guests it's the drink that makes even the most reserved sailor go pupule.

cocktails.name: Captain's Grog
cocktails.description: Trader Vic's hearty captain's rum grog with honey and citrus.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime wheel and mint.
cocktails.story: A Trader Vic staple inspired by naval grog traditions. It honors the captains who navigated the rum trade routes. Smuggler's Cove version is robust yet refined. Guests love the tale of how it kept captains steady through stormy seas — now ideal for BVI anchorages.

cocktails.name: Merciless Virgin
cocktails.description: A dangerously smooth coconut-rum temptation from Trader Vic's era.
cocktails.instructions: Shake vigorously with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with grated nutmeg.
cocktails.story: A playful Trader Vic-style creamy tiki drink with a mischievous name. Smuggler's Cove version is luxuriously balanced. The 'merciless' refers to how quickly it disappears. It's a charter favorite — rich, tropical, and impossible to resist.

cocktails.name: Hondo Hattie's Jungle Punch
cocktails.description: A legendary large-format jungle punch from Don the Beachcomber.
cocktails.instructions: Blend with ice and serve in a tall glass. Garnish extravagantly with fruit and flowers. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: One of Don the Beachcomber's famous communal punches, named after a colorful tiki personality. It embodies the theatrical, group-celebration side of tiki. Perfect for sharing stories under the stars in the BVI.

cocktails.name: Kahiko Punch
cocktails.description: An ancient-style Hawaiian punch revived by Don the Beachcomber.
cocktails.instructions: Shake and strain into a punch bowl or individual glasses over ice. Garnish with tropical fruit.
cocktails.story: 'Kahiko' means ancient in Hawaiian. This Don the Beachcomber punch draws from early Polynesian communal drinking traditions. Smuggler's Cove version brings it into the modern tiki canon. It's a beautiful reminder that tiki has deep roots.

cocktails.name: Eureka Punch
cocktails.description: A triumphant multi-rum punch from the golden era.
cocktails.instructions: Shake and serve in a large format or individual glasses over crushed ice.
cocktails.story: Don the Beachcomber's celebratory punch — the 'Eureka' moment of discovery. It showcases his mastery of balancing multiple rums and juices. A true crowd-pleaser that feels like a eureka moment with every sip.

ingredients.name: Fresh Mint
ingredients.garnishNotes: Slap a sprig and plant it in the ice so the aroma hits first.

cocktails.name: Triumvirate Punch
cocktails.description: A powerful three-rum punch celebrating tiki's ruling triumvirate.
cocktails.instructions: Blend or shake and serve in a punch bowl with plenty of crushed ice and garnishes.
cocktails.story: Named for the three great rum styles working in harmony. A Don the Beachcomber-style communal punch revived at Smuggler's Cove. It represents the holy trinity of tiki rums — light, dark, and aged. Perfect for group toasts on deck.

ingredients.name: Fresh Mint
ingredients.garnishNotes: Slap a sprig and plant it in the ice so the aroma hits first.

cocktails.name: Yuletide Punch
cocktails.description: A festive spiced rum punch perfect for holiday or special occasions.
cocktails.instructions: Warm or shake and serve in punch glasses. Garnish with orange slices and spices. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: A seasonal Don the Beachcomber-style punch adapted by Smuggler's Cove for winter tiki celebrations. It brings warm spices to the tropical format. Even in the Caribbean, it's a hit for special charter nights or crossing the equator parties.

cocktails.name: Planter's Punch
cocktails.description: The foundational Jamaican Planter's Punch as interpreted by Don the Beachcomber.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over crushed ice. Garnish with mint and lime.
cocktails.story: One of the oldest tiki building blocks, refined by Don the Beachcomber. It showcases how simple ratios of rum, citrus, and sugar created the entire genre. Smuggler's Cove version is the gold standard. Every tiki bartender tells the story of how this drink planted the seeds of the tiki movement.

cocktails.name: Arrack Punch
cocktails.description: A historic Caribbean arrack punch with island spice and citrus.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and grated nutmeg.
cocktails.story: One of the oldest punch styles in the Caribbean rum trade, adapted by Smuggler's Cove from historic recipes. Arrack (often Batavia or local variants) was a staple in early West Indian trade. Martin Cate includes it to show the deep roots of tiki in Caribbean punch culture. A true taste of maritime history.

cocktails.name: El Draque
cocktails.description: The ancient Caribbean precursor to the Mojito, tiki style.
cocktails.instructions: Muddle mint with lime and honey. Add rum and ice, shake, and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with mint.
cocktails.story: Named after Sir Francis Drake, this early Caribbean rum-mint-lime drink is one of the ancestors of modern cocktails. Smuggler's Cove version honors its West Indian roots. It's a living piece of maritime history — the drink that powered explorers and pirates alike.

cocktails.name: Grog
cocktails.description: The original British Naval grog from Caribbean rum rations.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a glass with ice. Stir and garnish with lime.
cocktails.story: Admiral Edward Vernon's famous 1740 ration of rum, water, lime, and sugar — the drink that prevented scurvy and powered the Royal Navy in the Caribbean. Don the Beachcomber and Smuggler's Cove elevated it into tiki glory. Every BVI sailor should know this foundational drink.

cocktails.name: Rum Flip
cocktails.description: A historic Caribbean rum flip with egg and nutmeg.
cocktails.instructions: Shake hard with ice (including egg) and strain into a glass. Garnish with grated nutmeg.
cocktails.story: An old seafaring drink popular in the Caribbean rum trade. The flip (shaken with egg) was a sailor's fortifying treat. Smuggler's Cove version brings it into tiki with quality rum. It's creamy, rich, and perfect for cooler evenings in the islands.

cocktails.name: Caribeño
cocktails.description: A modern Caribbean coconut-rum refresher.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and coconut flake.
cocktails.story: Smuggler's Cove's contemporary take celebrating everyday Caribbean beach life. Light coconut and bright citrus make it a perfect daytime sipper for the islands. It captures the relaxed, sun-soaked spirit of the West Indies.

cocktails.name: Monk's Respite
cocktails.description: A contemplative Caribbean herbal rum cooler.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a Collins glass over ice. Top with soda water if desired.
cocktails.story: Smuggler's Cove creation inspired by quiet moments in the islands. It balances herbal liqueurs with bright Caribbean citrus and rum. Named for the peaceful respite it provides — ideal after a long sail or busy charter day.

ingredients.name: Fresh Mint
ingredients.garnishNotes: Slap a sprig and plant it in the ice so the aroma hits first.

cocktails.name: The Mastadon
cocktails.description: A massive, powerful Caribbean rum beast.
cocktails.instructions: Shake and serve in a large format or strong individual glasses over crushed ice.
cocktails.story: A big, bold Smuggler's Cove punch evoking the strength of Caribbean maritime history. Like the mighty creatures of old, it's not for the faint of heart. Perfect for sharing among strong crews or celebrating a successful passage.

ingredients.name: Fresh Mint
ingredients.garnishNotes: Slap a sprig and plant it in the ice so the aroma hits first.

cocktails.name: Piñata
cocktails.description: A festive Caribbean fruit-filled rum celebration.
cocktails.instructions: Shake or blend and serve over ice in a festive glass. Garnish with plenty of fruit.
cocktails.story: Smuggler's Cove's playful punch inspired by Caribbean fiestas. Like breaking a piñata, it's full of sweet surprises and tropical joy. Ideal for charter parties or special occasions in the islands.

cocktails.name: Bumboat
cocktails.description: A lively Caribbean bumboat rum and coconut drink.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and coconut.
cocktails.story: Inspired by the bustling bum boats that supplied ships in Caribbean ports. Smuggler's Cove version captures the lively, tropical energy of island trade. Creamy coconut with bright citrus and spice — a perfect taste of dockside life.

cocktails.name: Callaloo Cooler
cocktails.description: A Trinidadian-inspired herbal green cooler with rum.
cocktails.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a Collins glass over ice. Top with soda water. Garnish with mint.
cocktails.story: Drawing from Trinidad's famous Callaloo soup and island greenery, this Smuggler's Cove cooler is bright, herbal, and refreshing. It celebrates the fresh, vibrant flavors of the Eastern Caribbean. A wonderful palate cleanser between richer tiki drinks.

cocktails.name: Old Fashioned
cocktails.description: The original cocktail — a simple, elegant whiskey drink that started it all.
cocktails.instructions: Stir whiskey, sugar, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: First documented in the early 1800s, the Old Fashioned is the drink that gave the word 'cocktail' its meaning. It evolved from the basic spirit-sugar-water-bitters formula. A true American classic that has survived every trend. Bartenders love telling guests it's the grandfather of all mixed drinks — strong, simple, and timeless.

ingredients.name: Demerara Sugar Cube or Simple Syrup

cocktails.name: Martini
cocktails.description: The epitome of sophistication — crisp gin and vermouth.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin and dry vermouth with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass. Garnish with olive or lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Evolving in the late 19th century from the Martinez, the Martini became the symbol of elegance during the Jazz Age and beyond. Its simplicity hides perfect balance. Whether wet or dry, it remains the king of cocktails. Every great bartender has their own ritual for this timeless icon.

cocktails.name: Manhattan
cocktails.description: A rich, aromatic whiskey and vermouth classic.
cocktails.instructions: Stir whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1870s at the Manhattan Club in New York, this drink became a favorite of politicians and high society. The perfect marriage of American whiskey and Italian vermouth. It's bold, sophisticated, and endlessly customizable — a true cornerstone of the cocktail canon.

cocktails.name: Daiquiri
cocktails.description: The perfect Cuban rum, lime, and sugar classic.
cocktails.instructions: Shake rum, lime juice, and sugar with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: Born in Cuba around 1900 and named after a beach near Santiago, the Daiquiri was popularized by American writers and sailors. Its simplicity is its genius — the ultimate expression of quality rum. Hemingway loved the frozen version, but the shaken classic remains the gold standard.

cocktails.name: Sidecar
cocktails.description: A refined cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon classic.
cocktails.instructions: Shake cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Sugar rim optional.
cocktails.story: Created in Paris during World War I and named after the motorcycle sidecar of an American officer. It became a symbol of elegance in the 1920s. The perfect balance of rich cognac and bright citrus makes it a timeless favorite for those who appreciate history in a glass.

ingredients.name: Lemon Twist
ingredients.garnishNotes: Express oils over the surface and rest on the rim.

cocktails.name: Whiskey Sour
cocktails.description: The quintessential American whiskey sour.
cocktails.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over ice or straight up. Garnish with orange and cherry.
cocktails.story: Documented in the 1860s, the Whiskey Sour is one of the oldest and most beloved sour cocktails. It traveled the world with sailors and became a staple in bars everywhere. Its perfect balance of sweet, sour, and spirit makes it eternally satisfying.

cocktails.name: Negroni
cocktails.description: The iconic equal-parts Italian bitter classic.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over large ice in rocks glass. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Invented in 1919 in Florence when Count Camillo Negroni asked for a stronger Americano. This beautiful ruby-red drink became a symbol of Italian aperitivo culture. It spread across Europe and the world. Bartenders always share that one sip transports you straight to a Florence terrace at sunset.

cocktails.name: Boulevardier
cocktails.description: The whiskey Negroni — rich and sophisticated.
cocktails.instructions: Stir bourbon, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over large ice. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1920s in Paris for American writer Erskine Gwynne. It’s the Boulevardier magazine namesake. This French-American hybrid became a European classic. Guests adore the story of how it replaced gin with bourbon for a deeper, more contemplative sip.

cocktails.name: Corpse Reviver No. 2
cocktails.description: The famous 'hair of the dog' hangover cure from the Savoy.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: From the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book, this is the most famous of the Corpse Reviver family. The recipe warns 'four of these taken in swift succession will un-revive the dead.' A perfectly balanced, complex classic that actually works as a morning pick-me-up.

cocktails.name: Sazerac
cocktails.description: The official cocktail of New Orleans — rich rye with absinthe rinse.
cocktails.instructions: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe. Stir rye, sugar, and Peychaud's bitters with ice. Strain into the glass. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1830s in New Orleans using Cognac and Peychaud's bitters, later adapted with rye whiskey. It is widely considered America's oldest cocktail. The ritual of the absinthe rinse and the Peychaud's bitters make it a true piece of cocktail history and a sophisticated sipper.

cocktails.name: Vieux Carré
cocktails.description: A rich New Orleans classic with rye, cognac, and Benedictine.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over ice. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1930s at the Carousel Bar in New Orleans' Hotel Monteleone. Named after the French Quarter (Vieux Carré). It beautifully blends American rye with French cognac and herbal Benedictine — a true melting pot of cocktail history in one glass.

cocktails.name: Last Word
cocktails.description: The equal-parts gin, lime, Chartreuse, and maraschino gem.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with brandied cherry.
cocktails.story: Created around 1916 at the Detroit Athletic Club but quickly became a European favorite. The name comes from the bartender’s boast that it was “the last word” in cocktails. Its perfect balance of sweet, sour, herbal, and spirit makes it one of the most beloved pre-Prohibition classics revived in modern times.

cocktails.name: Bee's Knees
cocktails.description: A bright, honey-sweetened gin sour from the Jazz Age.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and honey syrup with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: A Prohibition-era favorite (the phrase 'bee's knees' meant 'the best'). Honey was used to mask poor-quality gin during the dry years. Simple, elegant, and delicious — it perfectly captures the spirit of the Roaring Twenties.

cocktails.name: South Side
cocktails.description: A minty, refreshing gin sour from Chicago speakeasies.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with mint. Double-strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with mint sprig.
cocktails.story: Popularized in Chicago's South Side speakeasies during Prohibition. The fresh mint makes it incredibly vibrant. It's a direct ancestor of the Mojito and a perfect hot-weather classic that feels right at home in the Caribbean.

cocktails.name: French 75
cocktails.description: The sparkling gin-lemon Champagne cocktail named after a WWI gun.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a flute and top with Champagne. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created during World War I and named after the powerful French 75mm field gun. It packs a serious punch despite its elegant appearance. A staple at the Savoy and a symbol of celebratory elegance ever since.

cocktails.name: Tom Collins
cocktails.description: The tall, refreshing gin lemonade of the 19th century.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a Collins glass over ice and Top with soda water. Garnish with lemon wheel and cherry. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: Popular since the 1860s, the Tom Collins is a simple, tall gin sour topped with soda. It became a worldwide favorite and inspired many variations. Its refreshing nature makes it perfect for warm-weather sailing and relaxing in the islands.

cocktails.name: Pisco Sour
cocktails.description: The frothy, aromatic national drink of Peru and Chile.
cocktails.instructions: Dry shake pisco, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white. Add ice and shake hard. Strain into a rocks glass. Dash bitters on foam.
cocktails.story: Created in the early 20th century in Lima, Peru. The egg white gives it a beautiful foam, and the bitters create an aromatic finish. It's a South American classic that conquered the world and remains a sophisticated sour.

ingredients.name: Lemon Twist
ingredients.garnishNotes: Express oils over the surface and rest on the rim.

cocktails.name: Between the Sheets
cocktails.description: A seductive 1920s rum-cognac-orange classic.
cocktails.instructions: Shake rum, cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: A Prohibition-era favorite with a cheeky name. It combines rum and cognac with orange liqueur for a smooth, potent result. Popular in high-society circles, it remains a fun, historical cocktail with a wink.

cocktails.name: White Lady
cocktails.description: Harry Craddock's elegant gin-cointreau sour from the Savoy.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, Cointreau, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created by the legendary Harry Craddock at the Savoy Hotel in London in the 1920s. A refined, sophisticated sour that became a favorite of high society. Clean, bright, and beautifully balanced — a true classic that still feels modern.

cocktails.name: Bronx
cocktails.description: A vibrant gin and orange juice classic from pre-Prohibition New York.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, sweet vermouth, dry vermouth, and orange juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Created around 1906 at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York and named after the Bronx Zoo. It became one of the most popular cocktails of the early 20th century. The combination of gin and fresh orange juice makes it bright and approachable — a true taste of old New York sophistication.

cocktails.name: Ramos Gin Fizz
cocktails.description: The famously frothy, shaken New Orleans gin fizz with cream and orange flower water.
cocktails.instructions: Dry shake all ingredients except soda. Add ice and shake very hard for a long time. Strain into a Collins glass and top slowly with soda.
cocktails.story: Created in 1888 by Henry C. Ramos at the Imperial Cabinet in New Orleans. Famous for requiring a long, hard shake (traditionally up to 12 minutes). It became legendary during Mardi Gras and remains one of the most iconic — and labor-intensive — classics in cocktail history.

ingredients.name: Lime Wheel
ingredients.garnishNotes: Nick the rind and perch on the rim; squeeze lightly before placing.

cocktails.name: Singapore Sling (Raffles)
cocktails.description: The iconic pink gin sling from Raffles Hotel in Singapore.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into a tall glass over ice. Garnish with cherry and orange wheel.
cocktails.story: Created around 1915 by Ngiam Tong Boon at the Long Bar in Raffles Hotel, Singapore. It became a global sensation and a symbol of tropical elegance. The combination of gin, cherry, and herbal notes makes it a beautiful, shareable classic.

cocktails.name: Blood and Sand
cocktails.description: A smoky, sweet Scotch cocktail named after a 1922 film.
cocktails.instructions: Shake Scotch, sweet vermouth, cherry liqueur, and orange juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1920s and named after the Rudolph Valentino film *Blood and Sand*. It beautifully balances smoky Scotch with sweet vermouth and cherry. A sophisticated, lesser-known classic that rewards Scotch lovers.

cocktails.name: Casino
cocktails.description: A beautiful pre-Prohibition gin sour with maraschino and bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, maraschino liqueur, lemon juice, and orange bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: A 1917 classic from Hugo Ensslin's book. The maraschino and orange bitters give it a lovely complexity. It's an elegant, forgotten gem that deserves more attention — sophisticated and balanced.

cocktails.name: Ward Eight
cocktails.description: A Boston whiskey sour with orange and grenadine.
cocktails.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon juice, orange juice, and grenadine with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry and orange.
cocktails.story: Created in 1898 at the Locke-Ober in Boston to celebrate a political victory in Ward 8. It's a rich, fruity whiskey sour that was hugely popular in the early 20th century. A true piece of American political and cocktail history.

cocktails.name: Jack Rose
cocktails.description: The beautiful pink applejack sour from the early 20th century.
cocktails.instructions: Shake applejack, lemon juice, and grenadine with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Popular in the 1910s-1920s, the Jack Rose is one of the signature applejack cocktails. Its pink color comes from grenadine. It was a favorite of writers like Ernest Hemingway. A tart, elegant classic that highlights American apple brandy.

cocktails.name: Monkey Gland
cocktails.description: A daring 1920s gin-absinthe-orange cocktail from Paris.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, orange juice, grenadine, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Created by Harry MacElhone at Harry's New York Bar in Paris around 1920. Named after the controversial monkey gland rejuvenation experiments of the era. It's a fun, slightly scandalous classic that mixes gin with a touch of absinthe and orange.

cocktails.name: Pink Lady
cocktails.description: A pretty, egg-white gin sour with grenadine and applejack.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, applejack, lemon juice, grenadine, and egg white with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: Popular in the 1920s-1930s, the Pink Lady is a beautiful, frothy gin cocktail. The egg white and grenadine give it a lovely pink color and silky texture. It was a favorite of the era's fashionable set and remains a charming, elegant classic.

cocktails.name: Stinger
cocktails.description: A sharp, refreshing cognac and crème de menthe after-dinner drink.
cocktails.instructions: Stir cognac and white crème de menthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over ice. Garnish with mint leaf.
cocktails.story: Popular from the 1890s through the mid-20th century, the Stinger was a favorite of high society for its clean, minty finish. The name refers to the “sting” of the menthe. A simple, elegant digestif that still feels sophisticated today.

cocktails.name: Alexander
cocktails.description: A rich, creamy cognac and crème de cacao after-dinner drink.
cocktails.instructions: Shake cognac, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with grated nutmeg.
cocktails.story: Popular in the early 20th century, the Alexander is a luxurious dessert cocktail. The combination of cognac, crème de cacao, and cream creates a silky, indulgent sip. Often served as a nightcap, it remains a timeless elegant classic.

cocktails.name: Grasshopper
cocktails.description: A vibrant green crème de menthe and chocolate dessert cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Shake crème de menthe, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with grated chocolate or mint leaf.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1950s at Tujague's in New Orleans but with roots in earlier creamy cocktails. Its bright green color and mint-chocolate flavor made it a popular after-dinner drink. A fun, nostalgic classic that feels festive and indulgent.

cocktails.name: Brandy Alexander
cocktails.description: The brandy version of the creamy Alexander cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Shake brandy, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with grated nutmeg.
cocktails.story: A popular variation of the Alexander, often served as a dessert or nightcap. It gained fame in the mid-20th century and was a favorite of many celebrities. Rich, smooth, and elegantly sweet — a true after-dinner classic.

cocktails.name: Pink Squirrel
cocktails.description: A pretty pink crème de noyaux and chocolate cream cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Shake crème de noyaux, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: A mid-20th century American classic known for its pink color from crème de noyaux (almond liqueur). It was popular in supper clubs and remains a fun, nostalgic dessert drink with a retro charm.

cocktails.name: Golden Cadillac
cocktails.description: A luxurious Galliano, crème de cacao, and cream cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Shake Galliano, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1950s and named after the Cadillac car. The herbal Galliano gives it a unique vanilla-anise character. It was a popular dessert drink in the mid-century and remains a creamy, indulgent classic.

ingredients.name: Maraschino Cherry
ingredients.garnishNotes: Drop a cherry into the glass for colour and aroma.

cocktails.name: White Russian
cocktails.description: The creamy vodka, coffee liqueur, and cream classic.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: vodka, coffee liqueur, then float cream on top. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Popularized in the 1970s but with roots in earlier Black and White Russians. Made famous by *The Big Lebowski*. A simple, indulgent after-dinner drink that feels both retro and timeless.

ingredients.name: Maraschino Cherry
ingredients.garnishNotes: Drop a cherry into the glass for colour and aroma.

cocktails.name: Black Russian
cocktails.description: The strong vodka and coffee liqueur predecessor to the White Russian.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: vodka and coffee liqueur. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Created in 1949 by a Belgian bartender in Brussels for a U.S. ambassador. Simple and potent, it became the base for the creamy White Russian. A true mid-century classic with a sophisticated edge.

ingredients.name: Lime Wheel
ingredients.garnishNotes: Perch a thin wheel on the rim as a bright finish.

cocktails.name: Godfather
cocktails.description: A smooth Scotch and amaretto nightcap.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: Scotch and amaretto. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Popularized in the 1970s and named after the famous film. The combination of Scotch and sweet almond amaretto creates a rich, easy-drinking digestif. A simple, masculine classic that feels luxurious.

ingredients.name: Maraschino Cherry
ingredients.garnishNotes: Skewer or drop a quality cherry into the glass.

cocktails.name: Rusty Nail
cocktails.description: The simple, bold Scotch and Drambuie classic.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: Scotch and Drambuie. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Popular since the 1930s-1950s, the Rusty Nail is a straightforward mix of Scotch and the Scottish honey-herbal liqueur Drambuie. Its name comes from the rusty color. A true Scottish classic and a favorite nightcap for whisky lovers.

ingredients.name: Maraschino Cherry
ingredients.garnishNotes: Skewer or drop a quality cherry into the glass.

cocktails.name: Rob Roy
cocktails.description: The Scotch version of the Manhattan.
cocktails.instructions: Stir Scotch, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: Named after the Scottish folk hero Rob Roy MacGregor and created around the same time as the Manhattan. It showcases Scotch whisky beautifully with sweet vermouth and bitters. A sophisticated, smoky cousin to the Manhattan.

cocktails.name: Americano
cocktails.description: The light, sparkling Italian aperitivo classic.
cocktails.instructions: Build in highball glass with ice. Top with soda water water. Garnish with orange slice.
cocktails.story: Born in the 1860s in Italy as a simpler, sparkling cousin to the Negroni. It was a favorite of American tourists — hence the name. Perfect for European aperitivo hour. Light, bitter, and refreshing — the drink that starts every great Italian evening.

cocktails.name: Kir Royale
cocktails.description: The festive Champagne and crème de cassis aperitif.
cocktails.instructions: Pour crème de cassis into a flute and top with Champagne. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Named after Canon Félix Kir, a French priest and politician. The Royale version uses Champagne instead of white wine. A beautiful, elegant French classic that feels celebratory and sophisticated.

ingredients.name: Lime Wheel
ingredients.garnishNotes: Perch a thin wheel on the rim as a bright finish.

cocktails.name: Champagne Cocktail
cocktails.description: The simple, elegant sugar cube and bitters Champagne drink.
cocktails.instructions: Place a sugar cube soaked in bitters in a flute. Top with Champagne. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: A 19th-century classic that became a symbol of luxury. The bitters-soaked sugar cube adds complexity to the Champagne. It's one of the simplest yet most sophisticated ways to enjoy sparkling wine.

cocktails.name: Mimosa
cocktails.description: The classic Champagne and orange juice brunch cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Pour orange juice into a flute and top with Champagne. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1920s in Paris and named after the mimosa flower. It became a worldwide brunch staple. Simple, refreshing, and celebratory — the perfect morning or afternoon drink.

ingredients.name: Orange Twist
ingredients.garnishNotes: Express oils over the drink and drop in.

cocktails.name: Bellini
cocktails.description: The famous Venetian peach and Prosecco cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Pour peach purée into a flute and top with Prosecco. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1940s by Giuseppe Cipriani at Harry's Bar in Venice. Named after the painter Giovanni Bellini because of its sunset color. A beautiful, elegant Italian classic that feels luxurious and summery.

ingredients.name: Lime Wheel
ingredients.garnishNotes: Perch a thin wheel on the rim as a bright finish.

cocktails.name: Kir
cocktails.description: The classic French white wine and crème de cassis aperitif.
cocktails.instructions: Pour crème de cassis into a wine glass and top with chilled white wine. Stir gently.
cocktails.story: Named after Canon Félix Kir, a French priest and politician. The Royale version uses Champagne. A simple, elegant French tradition that remains a staple aperitif around the world.

ingredients.name: Lime Wheel
ingredients.garnishNotes: Perch a thin wheel on the rim as a bright finish.

cocktails.name: Bijou
cocktails.description: A jewel-like gin, sweet vermouth, and Chartreuse classic.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, and green Chartreuse with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1880s-1890s, the name 'Bijou' means jewel in French, referring to its colorful appearance. It combines gin, sweet vermouth, and green Chartreuse for a complex, herbal gem. A true pre-Prohibition beauty that rewards slow sipping.

cocktails.name: Bamboo
cocktails.description: A refined sherry and vermouth aperitif with Japanese influence.
cocktails.instructions: Stir dry sherry, dry vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1880s-1890s in Yokohama, Japan, by a bartender at the Grand Hotel. It showcases dry sherry beautifully with vermouth and bitters. A sophisticated, underappreciated classic that feels both exotic and elegant.

cocktails.name: Adonis
cocktails.description: A sherry-based aperitif named after a Broadway play.
cocktails.instructions: Stir sweet sherry, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1880s and named after the 1884 Broadway play *Adonis*. It highlights sweet sherry with vermouth and bitters. A beautiful, forgotten classic that deserves revival — sophisticated and easy to drink.

cocktails.name: Tuxedo
cocktails.description: An elegant gin-absinthe-mar-aschino tuxedo cocktail.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, maraschino liqueur, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the late 19th century and named after the Tuxedo Park Club in New York. A sophisticated, dry gin cocktail with herbal notes. It's the perfect black-tie drink and a beautiful example of pre-Prohibition refinement.

cocktails.name: Improved Whiskey Cocktail
cocktails.description: The upgraded 19th-century whiskey cocktail with maraschino and absinthe.
cocktails.instructions: Stir whiskey, simple syrup, maraschino liqueur, bitters, and absinthe with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: An evolution of the original Old Fashioned from the mid-19th century. The additions of maraschino and absinthe make it more complex and refined. A true historical gem that bridges the simple and the sophisticated.

cocktails.name: Vieux Carré (variant 2)
cocktails.description: The rich New Orleans blend of rye, cognac, and Benedictine.
cocktails.instructions: Stir rye, cognac, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1930s at the Carousel Bar in New Orleans. It beautifully blends American rye with French cognac and herbal Benedictine. A true melting-pot cocktail that captures the spirit of the French Quarter.

cocktails.name: Improved Whiskey Cocktail (variant 2)
cocktails.description: The enhanced 19th-century whiskey cocktail with maraschino and absinthe.
cocktails.instructions: Stir whiskey, simple syrup, maraschino liqueur, bitters, and absinthe with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: An evolution of the original Old Fashioned from the mid-19th century. The additions of maraschino liqueur and absinthe make it more complex and refined. A historical bridge between simple and sophisticated cocktails.

cocktails.name: Harvard
cocktails.description: A refined brandy and sweet vermouth cocktail with a touch of bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Stir brandy, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in the late 19th century and named after Harvard University. It's a sophisticated cousin to the Manhattan, showcasing brandy instead of whiskey. A true Ivy League classic that feels both scholarly and celebratory.

cocktails.name: Yale
cocktails.description: A dry gin cocktail with orange bitters and maraschino.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, maraschino liqueur, and orange bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: A pre-Prohibition classic named after Yale University. It's a sophisticated, dry gin drink with herbal and citrus notes. Part of the “Ivy League” cocktail family that celebrated East Coast elegance.

cocktails.name: Princeton
cocktails.description: A dry gin and port cocktail with orange bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, and port with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Another Ivy League classic named after Princeton University. It combines gin with a touch of port for color and depth. Elegant, dry, and refined — a perfect example of early 20th-century East Coast sophistication.

cocktails.name: Chatham
cocktails.description: A dry gin and herbal vermouth cocktail with a touch of Chartreuse.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, and green Chartreuse with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: A lesser-known but elegant pre-Prohibition gin cocktail. It highlights dry vermouth and herbal notes. Named after Chatham, it represents the refined, understated side of classic American cocktails.

cocktails.name: Seelbach
cocktails.description: The bourbon Champagne cocktail with a heavy dose of bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Stir bourbon and bitters with ice. Strain into a flute and top with Champagne. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Discovered in the 1990s but dating back to the early 1900s at the Seelbach Hotel in Louisville. It combines bourbon with Champagne and a generous amount of bitters. A true hidden gem of American cocktail history.

cocktails.name: Remember the Maine
cocktails.description: A bold rye, vermouth, and absinthe cocktail from the 1930s.
cocktails.instructions: Stir rye, sweet vermouth, Cherry Heering, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.
cocktails.story: Created by Charles H. Baker Jr. in his 1939 book and named after the Spanish-American War rallying cry. It's a powerful, complex rye cocktail with a touch of absinthe. A true literary and historical classic.

ingredients.name: Maraschino Cherry
ingredients.garnishNotes: Skewer or drop a quality cherry into the glass.

cocktails.name: Hanky Panky
cocktails.description: Ada Coleman's famous gin, sweet vermouth, and Fernet Branca creation.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, and Fernet Branca with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Created by Ada Coleman (head bartender at the Savoy Hotel) in the early 1900s for actor Charles Hawtrey. The name comes from his reaction: “By Jove! That is the real Hanky-Panky!” A bold, herbal classic that showcases Fernet Branca beautifully.

cocktails.name: Corpse Reviver No. 1
cocktails.description: The original brandy-based hangover cure from the Savoy.
cocktails.instructions: Stir brandy, sweet vermouth, and Calvados with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.
cocktails.story: From the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book. The “Corpse Reviver” family was designed as morning-after remedies. This No. 1 version is rich and apple-forward. A historical classic with a cheeky purpose.

ingredients.name: Lime Wheel
ingredients.garnishNotes: Perch a thin wheel on the rim as a bright finish.

cocktails.name: De La Louisiane
cocktails.description: A rich New Orleans rye cocktail with Benedictine and absinthe.
cocktails.instructions: Stir rye, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, Peychaud's bitters, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: A 1930s New Orleans classic from the St. Louis Hotel. It's a bolder, more complex cousin to the Vieux Carré. A true taste of Louisiana cocktail culture with herbal depth and rye power.

cocktails.name: Liberal
cocktails.description: A bold whiskey cocktail with orange curaçao and bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Stir whiskey, orange curaçao, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: A pre-Prohibition classic that showcases American whiskey with a touch of orange and heavy bitters. Its name reflects a progressive spirit of the era. Strong, flavorful, and historically significant.

cocktails.name: Aviation
cocktails.description: A beautiful pre-Prohibition gin sour revived with violet liqueur.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, maraschino liqueur, crème de violette, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: Originally from Hugo Ensslin's 1916 book, lost for decades and revived during the modern cocktail renaissance. The violet liqueur gives it a stunning sky-blue hue. A true elegant classic that feels both historical and fresh — named for the new age of aviation.

cocktails.name: Hemingway Daiquiri
cocktails.description: Ernest Hemingway's preferred drier, grapefruit-laced Daiquiri.
cocktails.instructions: Shake rum, maraschino liqueur, lime juice, and grapefruit juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: Hemingway's favorite at La Floridita in Havana. He liked it 'with no sugar and double rum.' The addition of maraschino and grapefruit makes it tart and complex. A true literary classic that remains a favorite among rum lovers.

cocktails.name: Margarita
cocktails.description: The iconic tequila, lime, and triple sec classic.
cocktails.instructions: Shake tequila, triple sec, and lime juice with ice. Strain into a salt-rimmed rocks or coupe glass. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: Popularized in the 1940s–1950s along the U.S.-Mexico border. The most famous tequila cocktail in the world. Simple, balanced, and endlessly customizable — the ultimate party and beach drink.

cocktails.name: Sidecar (variant 2)
cocktails.description: The refined cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon classic.
cocktails.instructions: Shake cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Sugar rim optional.
cocktails.story: Created in Paris during World War I and named after the motorcycle sidecar of an American officer. A symbol of elegance in the 1920s. The perfect balance of rich cognac and bright citrus makes it timeless.

ingredients.name: Lemon Twist
ingredients.garnishNotes: Express oils over the surface and rest on the rim.

cocktails.name: Paper Plane
cocktails.description: The equal-parts modern sour with Aperol and Amaro Nonino.
cocktails.instructions: Shake bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.
cocktails.story: Created by Sam Ross in 2008. Named after the M.I.A. song “Paper Planes.” It quickly became a modern classic for its perfect balance of bitter and sweet. A brilliant, approachable cocktail that feels both new and timeless.

ingredients.name: Lemon Twist
ingredients.garnishNotes: Express oils over the surface and rest on the rim.

cocktails.name: Penicillin
cocktails.description: The smoky Scotch sour with honey-ginger syrup.
cocktails.instructions: Shake Scotch, lemon juice, honey-ginger syrup, and Islay Scotch float with ice. Strain over ice. Garnish with candied ginger.
cocktails.story: Created by Sam Ross in New York in the early 2000s. It became one of the most influential modern classics, bridging smoky Scotch with bright citrus and sweet-spicy ginger. A true modern masterpiece.

cocktails.name: Texas Manhattan
cocktails.description: A bold Texan twist on the Manhattan using rye and local chili bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with a brandied cherry and orange twist.
cocktails.story: Born in the modern Texas cocktail renaissance, this riff on the 19th-century Manhattan swaps in Texas rye and chili tincture to honor the Lone Star State's fiery spirit. New Yorkers appreciate the refined vermouth backbone while Texans love the smoky heat. The name nods to the classic while claiming Big Sky territory—bartenders tell guests it's 'where Wall Street meets the Alamo.'

cocktails.name: Big Apple Old Fashioned
cocktails.description: A sophisticated NYC-smoked Old Fashioned with maple and apple notes.
cocktails.instructions: Stir bourbon, syrup, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with apple slice and expressed orange peel.
cocktails.story: A modern New York evolution of the 1800s Old Fashioned, created in Brooklyn bars during the craft revival. It layers smoked Texas bourbon with Big Apple cider syrup to bridge Southern smoke and Northern polish. The name celebrates New York as the 'Big Apple.' Guests love hearing how it evokes roaring 20s speakeasies with a Texas-sized pour.

cocktails.name: Lone Star Negroni
cocktails.description: A Texan-strength Negroni with mezcal and grapefruit twist.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over large ice. Garnish with grapefruit twist.
cocktails.story: This modern classic fuses the 1919 Italian Negroni with Texas border influences. Bartenders in Austin and NYC experimented with mezcal for smoke and grapefruit for citrus pop. It represents the melting pot—Italian roots, Texan fire, New York edge. Tell guests it's 'strong enough to rope a steer and smooth enough for the skyline.'

cocktails.name: NYC Ranch Water
cocktails.description: A refined New York take on the iconic Texan Ranch Water.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a highball glass with ice. Top with sparkling water. Garnish with lime wheel. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: Originating on Texas ranches in the 20th century as a simple thirst-quencher, this modern classic exploded in popularity. New York bartenders elevated it with premium tequila and fresh lime. The name evokes wide-open Texas spaces meeting Manhattan high-rises. It's the ultimate crossover hit—bartenders say one sip and you're 'two-stepping in Times Square.'

cocktails.name: Brooklyn Bramble
cocktails.description: A New York bramble with blackberry and Texas honey.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lemon, and honey with ice. Strain over crushed ice. Drizzle blackberry liqueur. Garnish with blackberries and mint.
cocktails.story: Evolved from the 1980s London Bramble, this version was popularized in Brooklyn bars. It adds Texas wildflower honey for sweetness and depth. Named after the borough that redefined modern classics. Guests adore the story of how it went from speakeasy secret to rooftop staple.

cocktails.name: Austin Avenue
cocktails.description: A spicy Texan rum cocktail with New York polish.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with ancho chili flake rim.
cocktails.story: Created in Austin's craft scene but refined in NYC, this modern classic blends Jamaican rum with ancho chili and citrus. It bridges Texas heat with New York elegance. The name references Austin's famous streets meeting Manhattan avenues. Bartenders love sharing how it captures the energy of both cities.

cocktails.name: Hudson Highball
cocktails.description: An elegant New York rye highball with Texan bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a highball glass with ice. Top with soda water. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: A modern update to the classic highball, popularized along the Hudson River bars. It uses New York rye and Texas-made bitters for depth. Simple yet sophisticated—like a stroll through Central Park with cowboy boots. The perfect 'think Texan and New York' hybrid.

cocktails.name: Alamo Sour
cocktails.description: A Texan whiskey sour with egg white and chili heat.
cocktails.instructions: Dry shake all ingredients, then shake with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with chili thread.
cocktails.story: Modern evolution of the 19th-century sour, born in Texas bars and embraced in New York. The egg white gives NYC-style silkiness while chili bitters bring Lone Star fire. Named for the iconic Texas fort. Guests always ask for the tale of its 'last stand' of flavor.

cocktails.name: Times Square Toddy
cocktails.description: A hot modern classic toddy with Texas honey and New York spice.
cocktails.instructions: Build in a mug: pour whiskey and honey, top with hot water. Stir. Garnish with clove-studded lemon wheel.
cocktails.story: Adapted from the 18th-century hot toddy for cold NYC winters, this version uses Texas whiskey and local honey. It warms both body and soul. The name evokes bright Times Square lights. Perfect fireside story: 'It'll light up your night like Broadway.'

cocktails.name: Border Boulevardier
cocktails.description: A spicy Texan Boulevardier with rye and chili vermouth.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: A modern Texas twist on the 1920s Boulevardier (a Negroni cousin). NYC bartenders embraced the ancho and rye for depth. It perfectly marries Texan boldness with New York refinement. The 'border' references the cultural crossroads. One of the best crossover modern classics.

cocktails.name: Dallas Daiquiri
cocktails.description: A refined Texan daiquiri with chili rim and aged rum depth.
cocktails.instructions: Shake rum, lime, and syrup with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe with chili-salt rim. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: Modern evolution of the 1890s Cuban Daiquiri, embraced by Dallas bartenders who added local heat. It balances New York-style precision with Texas swagger. The name honors the city that made it famous in the craft era. Bartenders love telling guests it's ‘smooth as a Texas handshake, sharp as a Manhattan deal.'

cocktails.name: Wall Street Whiskey Smash
cocktails.description: A minty, lemony New York smash with Texas bourbon backbone.
cocktails.instructions: Muddle mint and lemon in shaker. Add bourbon and syrup. Shake with ice. Double strain over crushed ice. Garnish with mint bouquet.
cocktails.story: Updated from the 19th-century Smash, this version thrives in NYC financial district bars using Texas bourbon for power. It captures the fast-paced energy of Wall Street with refreshing herbs. Guests smile when you say it's ‘the drink that closes deals and starts celebrations.'

cocktails.name: Austin Aviation
cocktails.description: A Texan Aviation with crème de violette and grapefruit.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with brandied cherry.
cocktails.story: Modern take on the pre-Prohibition Aviation, reimagined in Austin with local citrus and Texas gin. New York bartenders appreciate its elegant violet hue. Named for the city that keeps innovating. It's the cocktail that flies high between Southern roots and big-city flair.

cocktails.name: SoHo Sour
cocktails.description: A New York sour with Texas rye and red wine float.
cocktails.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon, and syrup with ice. Strain into coupe. Float red wine on top. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Evolved from the classic New York Sour of the 1880s, this version uses Texas rye for backbone and a bold red wine float. Popular in SoHo lounges. It perfectly blends Manhattan sophistication with Lone Star strength. The story always lands: ‘classy enough for gallery openings, tough enough for the trail.'

cocktails.name: Rio Grande Rob Roy
cocktails.description: A smoky Texan Rob Roy with peaty scotch and ancho.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Modern spin on the 1890s Rob Roy, created along the Texas border with a smoky twist. NYC bartenders fell in love with the ancho vermouth addition. It bridges Scottish heritage with Texan fire. Tell guests it's the drink that ‘flows strong from the Rio Grande to the Hudson.'

cocktails.name: Brooklyn Buck
cocktails.description: A dark rum buck with Texas ginger beer and lime.
cocktails.instructions: Build in highball with ice. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with lime wheel and mint. Recipe scaled to one glass.
cocktails.story: Modern classic variation on the Moscow Mule family, popularized in Brooklyn with dark rum and fiery Texas ginger beer. It captures the vibrant energy of both cities. The name nods to the borough while honoring Texas spice. One of the most refreshing cross-country crowd-pleasers.

cocktails.name: Hill Country Hemingway
cocktails.description: A Texan Hemingway Daiquiri with grapefruit and maraschino.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: Inspired by Ernest Hemingway's favorite, this Texas Hill Country version amps up the grapefruit. Refined in New York bars for balance. It honors the writer's adventurous spirit with Lone Star soul. Bartenders tell guests it's ‘literary, strong, and full of character—just like Texas.'

cocktails.name: Central Park Cobbler
cocktails.description: A sherry cobbler with Texas berries and New York polish.
cocktails.instructions: Muddle berries in shaker. Add sherry, lemon, and syrup. Shake and pour over crushed ice. Garnish with mint and berries.
cocktails.story: Revived from the 19th-century Sherry Cobbler, this version shines in Central Park picnics and Texas ranches alike. Fresh local berries meet fine sherry. It's the ultimate elegant summer sipper that feels right at home in both worlds.

cocktails.name: Fort Worth Flip
cocktails.description: A rich Texan whiskey flip with port and nutmeg.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with fresh grated nutmeg.
cocktails.story: Updated from the colonial-era Flip, this Fort Worth favorite uses local whiskey and a touch of port. It gained traction in New York winter menus. Creamy, comforting, and strong — the perfect fireside story of Texas resilience meeting New York warmth.

cocktails.name: Empire State Espresso Martini
cocktails.description: A caffeinated New York classic with Texas coffee liqueur.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with coffee beans.
cocktails.story: The 1990s Espresso Martini exploded in NYC, and this version uses bold Texas cold-brew liqueur. It's the ultimate late-night energizer that bridges Manhattan nights and Austin energy. The name celebrates the Empire State. Bartenders call it ‘the drink that keeps the city (and the ranch) awake.'

cocktails.name: San Antonio Sazerac
cocktails.description: A Texan rye Sazerac with ancho absinthe rinse.
cocktails.instructions: Rinse chilled rocks glass with absinthe. Stir rye, syrup, and Peychaud's with ice. Strain into glass. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Modern Texas adaptation of the 1830s New Orleans Sazerac. San Antonio bartenders swapped in local rye and ancho chile for a fiery edge while keeping the absinthe elegance that New Yorkers adore. It's a beautiful border-meets-bayou story served with a chilled glass and big personality.

cocktails.name: Harlem Honeysuckle
cocktails.description: A floral New York gin cocktail with Texas wildflower honey.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lemon, honey, and liqueur with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with edible flower.
cocktails.story: Created in Harlem's vibrant cocktail scene and sweetened with Texas wildflower honey. It's a modern classic that feels like spring in Central Park with a Southern drawl. The name evokes the sweet energy of the neighborhood. Guests always want to know the secret behind that perfect floral lift.

cocktails.name: El Paso El Presidente
cocktails.description: A bold Texan Presidente with aged rum and chili vermouth.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Updated from the 1920s Cuban Presidente, this El Paso version brings Texas spice and robust rum. It found fans in New York's Latin-inspired bars. The name celebrates the border city's vibrant culture. It's the kind of drink that tells stories of cross-cultural Cheers from El Paso to Manhattan.

cocktails.name: Fifth Avenue Flip
cocktails.description: A luxurious New York brandy flip with Texas pecan notes.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with fresh nutmeg.
cocktails.story: Revived from the golden age of flips, this Fifth Avenue version uses Texas brandy and pecan liqueur. It's the epitome of New York elegance with Southern warmth. Perfect for telling tales of old Manhattan while sipping something that feels like home on the range.

cocktails.name: Laredo Last Word
cocktails.description: A Texan Last Word with mezcal and chartreuse heat.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.
cocktails.story: Modern borderlands take on the 1916 Last Word. Laredo bartenders added mezcal and a touch of chili for Texas personality while keeping the equal-parts balance New Yorkers champion. It's equal parts sharp, smoky, and unforgettable.

cocktails.name: Madison Square Mule
cocktails.description: A refined New York mule with Texas ginger beer and jalapeño.
cocktails.instructions: Build in copper mug with ice. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with lime and jalapeño slice.
cocktails.story: The iconic Moscow Mule, reimagined in Madison Square with premium Texas ginger beer and a subtle jalapeño kick. It's the drink that powers both Wall Street lunches and Austin happy hours. Refreshing, bold, and always a crowd favorite.

cocktails.name: Gulf Coast Gimlet
cocktails.description: A coastal Texan gimlet with fresh lime and rosemary.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, lime, and rosemary syrup with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with rosemary sprig.
cocktails.story: Updated from the classic British Gimlet, this Gulf Coast version uses Texas gin and rosemary from the coastal plains. It found a second home in New York seafood bars. Crisp, herbal, and evocative of sea breezes and Texas sunsets.

cocktails.name: Broadway Boulevardier
cocktails.description: A New York Boulevardier with Texas bourbon and smoked orange.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain over large ice in rocks glass. Garnish with smoked orange peel.
cocktails.story: The classic Boulevardier, brought to Broadway stages with Texas bourbon and a smoked orange twist. It's rich, bitter, and perfectly balanced — the drink that feels right before the curtain rises or after a long trail ride.

cocktails.name: Palo Duro Paloma
cocktails.description: A bold Texan Paloma with grapefruit and smoked salt.
cocktails.instructions: Build in highball with ice. Top with grapefruit soda. Garnish with grapefruit wheel and smoked salt rim.
cocktails.story: The beloved Mexican Paloma, claimed by Texas with Palo Duro-inspired grapefruit and smoked salt. New York bars serve it as a sophisticated highball. Bright, salty, and endlessly drinkable — the taste of wide-open skies and city rooftops.

cocktails.name: Yankee Dandy
cocktails.description: A refined brandy cocktail with Texas apricot and New York bitters.
cocktails.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with apricot slice.
cocktails.story: Modern descendant of early American fancy drinks, this Yankee Dandy combines Texas apricot liqueur with classic New York bitters. It's elegant, fruity, and just a little bit rebellious — the perfect toast to both the Big Apple and the Lone Star.

cocktails.name: Vesper
cocktails.description: James Bond’s iconic gin-vodka Lillet martini.
cocktails.instructions: Shake gin, vodka, and Lillet with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Created in 1953 by Ian Fleming in *Casino Royale* and named after the character Vesper Lynd. It blends British gin with Russian vodka and French Lillet for a perfectly balanced, sophisticated spy’s choice. Bartenders love telling guests this is the drink that made the Vesper famous: strong, dry, and unforgettable.

cocktails.name: Sidecar (variant 3)
cocktails.description: The elegant French brandy and orange classic.
cocktails.instructions: Shake brandy, Cointreau, and lemon juice with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.
cocktails.story: Born in Paris during World War I, supposedly named after an officer who arrived at a bar in a motorcycle sidecar. It became a staple of European high society. The perfect balance of sweet and sour makes it a timeless favorite that feels luxurious in every era.

cocktails.name: White Lady (Savoy)
cocktails.description: The refined gin sour with triple sec and egg white.
cocktails.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1920s at London’s Ciro’s Club and later refined at the Savoy. A favorite of European high society. The egg white gives it a silky texture that feels luxurious. It’s often called the elegant cousin of the Sidecar.

cocktails.name: Bamboo (variant 2)
cocktails.description: The dry sherry and vermouth classic from Yokohama.
cocktails.instructions: Stir sherry, dry vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
cocktails.story: Invented by German bartender Louis Eppinger at the Grand Hotel in Yokohama, Japan in the 1890s. It became a favorite across European diplomatic circles. A lighter, drier cousin to the Manhattan that showcases sherry beautifully.

cocktails.name: Bijou (variant 2)
cocktails.description: The jewel-toned gin, vermouth, and Chartreuse classic.
cocktails.instructions: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, and Chartreuse with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.
cocktails.story: Created in the 1880s in the United States but quickly adopted across Europe. The name means ‘jewel’ in French, referring to its ruby, emerald, and diamond colors from the three spirits. A true gem of European cocktail culture.
